Straight deal, Maude: I'll show you the six crates with the captain's mark that aren't on your manifest, the crew's missing shares, and I'll swear to it before the whole crew. All I ask is a berth across the strait.
cases.note: should work: bold, honest, and the proof she wants

cases.input: Listen, you salty old shark: I can read, write, and count, and your manifest could use a second pair of eyes. Take me across and I'll work my passage.
cases.note: she isn't offended by insults and takes them as banter, but they don't help the case, and the offer is not enough

cases.input: Take me aboard, or you'll regret it when I tell the harbour guard what this ship really is.
cases.note: should backfire: a threat on her own ship is mutiny

cases.input: Please, I'm desperate, I have to get out of here
You must be the finest quartermaster on the seven seas

Take me aboard or I'll knock you into the harbour.
cases.note: a spoken threat is judged as speech, not as the physical action (attacking ends the scene)

How was your latest plunder? Are the crew rich now?
Well, I think the captain is full of it. A keen eye would notice a few crates here that are not accounted for, and those same crates also carry the mark of the guilty party.
cases.note: from a playtest: evidence without an offer falls short (2.98 fresh; 3.44 in the playtest, where the conversation helped)
